old: A ranking only: it can compare two flow rates and cannot be interpreted as a fraction at all.
new: A ranking only, useful to compare two flow rates and nothing more.

old: All of them.
new: All of them, since each one acts through the annulus.

old: The cuttings volume at the shakers.
new: The cuttings volume at the shakers, compared against what the bit is cutting at that moment.

old: Nothing connects them.
new: Nothing connects them, since one course models pressure and the other models forces.

old: Rotation and pipe movement.
new: Rotation and pipe movement, which both stir the annulus.

old: Valid for any inclination, since the slip velocity is a property of the particle and the fluid rather than of the geometry.
new: Valid at any inclination, as slip is a property of particle and fluid alone.

old: Valid only for the two wells in the fixture set, since the goldens contain no other geometry to check it against.
new: Valid only for the two fixture wells, since the goldens hold no other geometry.

old: Because the ECD is computed with a margin already built in, so it appears more comfortable than it is.
new: Because the ECD is computed with a margin built in, so it looks more comfortable.

old: The mud is too thin, the annulus too wide or the rate of penetration too high for any rate to keep up.
new: The mud is too thin, the annulus too wide or the penetration rate too high.

old: The mud weight.
new: The mud weight, through its density.

old: The equivalent circulating density.
new: The equivalent circulating density, since a wider nozzle sends more pressure to the annulus.

old: The mud first, since it is the input most easily changed at the rig and it affects both constraints at once.
new: The mud first, as it is easiest to change at the rig.

old: The string's bore first, since it is the largest lever on pump pressure by a considerable margin.
new: The string's bore first, being the largest lever.

old: The nozzle area affects the equivalent circulating density, so it has to be fixed before the ECD check can be made.
new: The nozzle area affects the ECD, so it must be fixed before the ECD check.

old: The nozzle area affects the cleaning through the jet velocity, so the two decisions cannot be separated at all.
new: The nozzles affect cleaning through the jet, so the two decisions are inseparable.

old: A laboratory flow loop.
new: A laboratory flow loop, in which the same mud is pumped through a pipe and annulus of known geometry at a range of rates.

old: Within one part in a million.
new: Within one part in a million, which is the same agreement the two implementations reach with each other.

old: The method specification, the software version, the date and the engineer, which is what a fitted parameter needs.
new: The method specification, the software version, the date and the engineer who ran it.

old: The transport ratio.
new: The transport ratio, since it compares two velocities of the same annulus.

old: The two circulating densities.
new: The two circulating densities, since both wells share one mud.

old: That the pump binds before the formation does on most wells, which is why the ECD is rarely the constraint.
new: That the pump binds before the formation does on most wells, so the ECD rarely binds.

old: The geomechanics that produce the pore pressure and the fracture gradient this tier compared against.
new: The geomechanics behind the pore and fracture limits.

new: The transient effects the steady-state model omits.

new: Always use the highest flow rate, since the ECD rises so little with rate.
